newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Prices soft on bearish palm, soyoil.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Prices soft on bearish palm, soyoil.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to slide this week as the market is likely to be swamped by the bearish influence of other vegetable oils such as palm and soy oil, Manila-based vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"Prices will be softer due to the continuing bearish influence of palm and soybean oil," said one Manila trader.
Another trader said a lack of aggressive buyers and a possible increase in Philippine copra supply in the next few weeks due to improving weather could dampen prices.
Indonesian and Malaysian traders have said they expect palm oil prices to fall this week due to ample supplies and poor export prospects.
"Because of pressure from palm oil and soyoil and lack of fresh news to bouy up the market, we will likely see range-bound trading next week," a Manila trader said.
The October soyoil contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) closed on Friday 0.08 U.S. cents down at 22.82 a lb.
Philippine coconut oil faces competition from palm oil exported by Indonesia and Malaysia and from soy oil, mostly from the United States.
UCAP said the Philippines exported 63,257 tonnes of coconut oil and 12,500 tonnes copra meal from October 1 to 17.
"I expect coconut oil prices to be range-bound, moving between the $10 to $15 area," said one trader.

The private trade group United Coconut Associations of the Philippine (UCAP) said sellers were offering coconut oil for November/December shipment at an average US$716.25 per tonne CIF Europe in early Monday trade.
Buyers for November/December quoted an average price of $707.50 a tonne, UCAP said.
Coconut oil prices for forward shipments, on the other hand, are expect to fall below the $700 per tonne CIF from the current level of $710, traders said.
